# Cloud Custodian

The **Cloud Custodian Plugin** runs Cloud Custodian policies in dry-run mode,
builds a full inventory baseline for each configured resource type, converts
each resource/policy pair into a standardized per-resource payload, and then
executes CCF OPA bundles against those payloads to generate evidence.

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-cloud-custodian` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.3.0](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-cloud-custodian/releases/tag/v0.3.0) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.3.0](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-cloud-custodian/blob/v0.3.0/README.md).

## How it works

### Behavior Overview

1. Load Cloud Custodian policy YAML from config.
2. Parse top-level `policies` and iterate one policy entry per check.
3. Register runtime-derived subject templates for each configured resource type during runner-v2 `Init`.
4. Run one unfiltered inventory collection for each unique resource type.
5. Run each configured check with:

```bash
custodian run --dryrun -s <output-dir> <single-policy-file>
```

6. Compare each check's matched resources with the inventory baseline.
7. Build one standardized payload per resource per check. Matched resources are marked `non_compliant`; baseline resources not matched by that check are marked `compliant`.
8. Evaluate each OPA policy bundle path from agent `EvalRequest.policyPaths`.
9. Send evidence via the plugin gRPC helper (`CreateEvidence`).

### Safety Model

This plugin always enforces read-only Cloud Custodian execution:

- `--dryrun` is always used.
- Mutating actions are not applied.
- For AWS checks, the plugin runs with `--region all` to evaluate across all AWS regions by default unless `aws_regions` is configured.
- With more than one region (including `all`), Cloud Custodian writes one `resources.json` per region (`<output>/<region>/<policy>/resources.json`). The plugin reads every one of them, for the inventory baseline and for each check.
- On execution failures or timeouts, the plugin includes the tail of any generated `custodian-run.log` artifacts in the execution error.

## Requirements

### Operational Prerequisites

- Cloud Custodian CLI must be installed and executable.
- Cloud/provider credentials must be available in the plugin process environment
  (ambient credentials/profile/env vars). With `aws_accounts`, these are the hub's
  credentials, used to assume each account's role.

## Configuration

All plugin config fields are strings (agent gRPC `map<string,string>` contract).

| Key | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `policies_yaml` | Conditionally | Inline Cloud Custodian policy YAML. Preferred over `policies_path` when both are set. |
| `policies_path` | Conditionally | Local path, `file://`, `http://`, or `https://` location for policy YAML. Used when `policies_yaml` is empty. |
| `custodian_binary` | No | Path/name of Cloud Custodian executable. Default: `custodian`. |
| `custodian_debug` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to pass `--debug` to Cloud Custodian. This increases Cloud Custodian diagnostic output on stderr. Default: `false`. |
| `custodian_verbose` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to pass `-v` to Cloud Custodian. This increases Cloud Custodian diagnostic output on stderr. Default: `false`. |
| `custodian_aws_api_trace` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to inject a temporary Python `sitecustomize.py` into the Custodian child process. Logs botocore API start/end/error events to stderr and `custodian-aws-api-trace.jsonl` in the check output directory. Default: `false`. |
| `custodian_network_diagnostics` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to run Go DNS/TLS preflight probes for relevant AWS service endpoints before Custodian starts and log child process TCP socket snapshots while Custodian is running. DNS/TLS probe failures are logged as warnings and surfaced in evidence as `execution.warnings`. Concrete `aws_regions` are narrowed to regions with reachable resource service endpoints before Custodian runs; if none are reachable for a check, that check is skipped, later checks continue, and the accumulated diagnostic warnings are returned after reachable evidence is submitted. If no concrete `aws_regions` are configured, service-derived probes are skipped unless `custodian_network_diagnostic_endpoints` is configured. For AWS resource types not mapped to diagnostic services, diagnostics warn and continue unless explicit endpoints are configured. Invalid configured endpoints still fail before execution. Default: `false`. |
| `custodian_network_diagnostic_endpoints` | No | Comma or whitespace separated list of additional endpoint hostnames, `host:port` values, or HTTPS URLs to DNS/TLS probe when `custodian_network_diagnostics` is enabled. Non-HTTPS URL schemes are rejected. Use this for AWS VPC endpoint DNS names such as `vpce-123.backup.eu-west-1.vpce.amazonaws.com`. Default: unset. |
| `custodian_log_tail_during_run` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to tail discovered `custodian-run.log` artifacts during the monitor loop, not only after process exit. Default: `false`. |
| `aws_regions` | No | Comma or whitespace separated AWS regions passed as repeated `--region` flags. Duplicate entries are removed while preserving order. Default: unset, which falls back to `--region all` for AWS checks. |
| `check_timeout_seconds` | No | Per-check timeout in seconds. Default: `300`. |
| `policy_labels` | No | JSON map of labels merged into generated evidence labels. |
| `resource_identity_fields` | No | JSON object mapping Cloud Custodian resource types to ordered identity field paths. Built-in defaults (see [Resource Identity](#resource-identity)) are used after configured fields. Example: `{"aws.ec2":["InstanceId","Arn"]}`. |
| `debug_dump_payloads` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to write standardized resource payload JSON files for troubleshooting. Default: `false`. |
| `debug_payload_output_dir` | No | Directory where debug payload JSON files are written. If set, debug dumping is auto-enabled. Default when enabled without explicit path: `ccf-custodian-debug-payloads` under the OS temp directory (`$TMPDIR`, else `/tmp`), e.g. `/tmp/ccf-custodian-debug-payloads`. Use an absolute path: a relative value is still honoured but resolves against the plugin process working directory (which the agent may set per plugin) and logs a warning. The resolved absolute path is logged at `INFO` when dumping is enabled. |
| `preserve_execution_artifacts` | No | Boolean (`true`/`false`) toggle to keep the temporary Cloud Custodian execution root after a check execution failure for postmortem review. Default: `false`. |
| `aws_accounts` | No | JSON (or YAML) array of AWS accounts to scan: `{"id", "name", "role_arn", "role_name", "external_id", "regions", "use_ambient_credentials"}`, only `id` required. See [Cross-Account Scanning](#cross-account-scanning). Default: unset, which scans the account of the plugin's own credentials. |
| `aws_assume_role_name` | No | Role name assumed in every account without its own `role_arn` or `role_name`. Only used with `aws_accounts`. |
| `aws_external_id` | No | External ID passed when assuming a role in an account without its own `external_id`. Only used with `aws_accounts`. Never logged. |
| `aws_partition` | No | Partition of the role ARNs built from role names (`aws`, `aws-cn`, `aws-us-gov`, ...). Only used with `aws_accounts`. Default: derived from the account's regions (`cn-*` is `aws-cn`, `us-gov-*` is `aws-us-gov`), else `aws`. |
| `aws_session_name_suffix` | No | Suffix of the STS session name, `CloudCustodian@<suffix>` (`C7N_SESSION_SUFFIX`). Only used with `aws_accounts`. Default: `ccf`. |

Validation rules:

- At least one of `policies_yaml` or `policies_path` must be provided.
- `custodian_binary` must resolve on PATH (or as explicit executable path).
- `check_timeout_seconds` must be a positive integer.
- `resource_identity_fields`, when set, must be valid JSON and each resource type must include at least one field path.
- Policy YAML must include top-level `policies` array.
- With `aws_accounts`: every account `id` is 12 digits and listed once; each account has a role (`role_arn`, `role_name` or `aws_assume_role_name`) or `use_ambient_credentials: true`, but not its own role and ambient credentials together, and at most one account uses ambient credentials; a `role_arn` belongs to its account; an external ID is 2 to 1224 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9_+=,.@:/-]`; unknown account keys are rejected; every policy is an AWS policy. Without `aws_accounts`, the other `aws_*` account keys are ignored with a warning.

### Example Agent Config (Inline YAML)

```yaml
plugins:
  cloud_custodian:
    source: ./dist/plugin
    policies:
      - ./policy-bundle
    config:
      policies_yaml: |
        policies:
          - name: ec2-public-ip-check
            resource: aws.ec2
            filters:
              - type: value
                key: PublicIpAddress
                op: not-null
      custodian_binary: custodian
      check_timeout_seconds: "300"
      policy_labels: '{"team":"cloud-security","environment":"prod"}'
```

### Example Agent Config (Path/URL Fallback)

```yaml
plugins:
  cloud_custodian:
    source: ./dist/plugin
    policies:
      - ./policy-bundle
    config:
      policies_path: file:///etc/ccf/cloud-custodian.yaml
      custodian_binary: /usr/local/bin/custodian
```

### Cross-Account Scanning

Without `aws_accounts` the plugin scans the account of its own (ambient) credentials, exactly as before. With
`aws_accounts`, it scans only the listed accounts, one after the other, assuming a role in each through Cloud
Custodian's `--assume` and `--external-id`. The account the plugin runs in (the hub) is scanned only when it is
listed with `use_ambient_credentials: true`. Its `id` is checked against the accounts in the ARNs of the resources it
finds: if they name another account, the hub fails and submits no evidence (the other accounts still run); if no ARN
names an account, the plugin logs a warning that it can't verify the id.

For each account:

- the role is the entry's `role_arn`, else `arn:<partition>:iam::<id>:role/<role_name>`, else the same with
  `aws_assume_role_name`;
- the external ID is the entry's `external_id`, else `aws_external_id`;
- the regions are the entry's `regions`, else `aws_regions`, else `all`.

```yaml
plugins:
  cloud_custodian:
    source: ghcr.io/compliance-framework/plugin-cloud-custodian:<version>
    policies:
      - ghcr.io/compliance-framework/plugin-cloud-custodian-policies:<version>
    config:
      policies_path: file:///etc/ccf/cloud-custodian.yaml
      aws_regions: "eu-west-1,us-east-1"
      aws_assume_role_name: ccf-audit
      aws_external_id: "${env:CCF_CUSTODIAN_EXTERNAL_ID}"
      aws_accounts: |
        [
          {"id": "111111111111", "name": "hub", "use_ambient_credentials": true},
          {"id": "222222222222", "name": "prod", "role_name": "ccf-prod-audit", "external_id": "${env:CCF_PROD_EXTERNAL_ID}"},
          {"id": "333333333333", "name": "dev", "regions": ["eu-west-1"]},
          {"id": "444444444444", "name": "legacy", "role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::444444444444:role/security/ccf-audit"}
        ]
```

Here the hub uses the agent's own credentials; prod assumes `ccf-prod-audit` with its own external ID; dev assumes
`ccf-audit` with the global external ID in `eu-west-1` only; legacy assumes the given role with the global external ID. The agent resolves the
`${env:...}` placeholders before the plugin sees them.

What changes in accounts mode:

- The `account_id` label is the scanned account, whatever the resource data says, and `account_name` is added when the
  account has a `name`. Both are reserved: `policy_labels` can't set them.
- The payload gets `"account": {"id": "...", "name": "..."}`, and `resource.account_id` is the scanned account.
- `account_id` is part of the evidence UUID seed and of the resource subject id
  (`cloud-custodian-resource/<account>/<type>/<id>`), and the subject templates' identity keys are
  `provider`, `account_id`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`. The same resource id in two accounts is two resources.
  Moving an existing deployment to `aws_accounts` therefore re-keys its evidence streams once. `account_name` is
  not part of the seed, so renaming an account keeps its evidence streams.
- Each account has its own inventory baseline, Cloud Custodian cache file and output directory.

When an account fails (for example its role can't be assumed, which skips the account's remaining runs), the other
accounts still run and submit their evidence. The run then fails with one error whose first line names every failed
account, followed, per account, by its role, its errors and the tail of Cloud Custodian's output. The agent records that
error as the plugin run's error (its log and the agent run evidence).

#### Regions

With `all` (no `regions` and no `aws_regions`), Cloud Custodian lists the enabled regions with the hub's credentials
(`ec2:DescribeRegions`), not the target account's, so an opt-in region enabled only in a target account is missed. The
plugin logs a warning for each such account; list the regions to scan them. On private networks without a route to the
global STS endpoint, set `C7N_USE_STS_REGIONAL=true` in the agent's environment so Cloud Custodian assumes roles through
the regional STS endpoint (for example a VPC endpoint).

#### IAM

- The hub principal (the plugin's own credentials) needs `sts:AssumeRole` on the target roles. Narrow it to them, for
  example with an `aws:ResourceOrgID` condition or a list of the role ARNs, plus `ec2:DescribeRegions` when any account
  scans `all` regions.
- Each target role trusts the hub principal with an `sts:ExternalId` condition, and can also require the session name:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/ccf-agent"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": {
      "StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "<external id>"},
      "StringLike": {"sts:RoleSessionName": "CloudCustodian@ccf*"}
    }
  }]
}
```

- The target role's permissions are the AWS managed policies `SecurityAudit` and `job-function/ViewOnlyAccess`, not
  `ReadOnlyAccess`, which can also read data (S3 objects, DynamoDB items, secrets).

#### Remote configuration

Never list `aws_accounts`, `aws_assume_role_name`, `aws_external_id`, `aws_partition` or `aws_session_name_suffix` in
the agent's `remote_config.overridable_config_flags` (and don't use `*` there for this plugin): a remote
overlay could then point the plugin at other accounts or roles without an operator's review.

| Bundle | Latest version | Controls covered | Compatible plugin lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`plugin-cloud-custodian-policies`](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-cloud-custodian-policies) | `v0.2.2` | *none listed* | latest |

### Standardized Per-Resource OPA Input

Each resource/check iteration produces one payload with this shape:

```json
{
  "schema_version": "v2",
  "source": "cloud-custodian",
  "check": {
    "name": "ec2-public-ip-check",
    "resource": "aws.ec2",
    "provider": "aws",
    "index": 0,
    "metadata": {}
  },
  "resource": {
    "id": "i-1234567890abcdef0",
    "type": "aws.ec2",
    "provider": "aws",
    "account_id": "123456789012",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "identity_fields": {
      "InstanceId": "i-1234567890abcdef0"
    },
    "data": {"...": "..."}
  },
  "assessment": {
    "status": "non_compliant",
    "matched": true,
    "inventory_status": "baseline",
    "matched_resource_count": 3,
    "artifact_path": "/tmp/ccf-cloud-custodian-123/001-ec2-public-ip-check",
    "resources_path": "/tmp/ccf-cloud-custodian-123/001-ec2-public-ip-check/ec2-public-ip-check/resources.json"
  },
  "execution": {
    "status": "success",
    "dry_run": true,
    "exit_code": 0,
    "started_at": "2026-03-06T12:00:00Z",
    "ended_at": "2026-03-06T12:00:01Z",
    "duration_ms": 1000,
    "stdout": "...",
    "stderr": "",
    "error": "",
    "errors": []
  },
  "raw_policy": {
    "name": "ec2-public-ip-check",
    "resource": "aws.ec2",
    "filters": []
  }
}
```

Generated evidence labels include `resource_id`, `resource_type`, `provider`,
and any available `account_id`/`region` (with `aws_accounts`: the scanned
account's `account_id`, its `account_name`, and an `account` object in the
payload, see [Cross-Account Scanning](#cross-account-scanning)). A region in the resource data is used
as is; otherwise, when Cloud Custodian wrote per-region output, `region` is the
region directory the resource came from. Global resource types (IAM, CloudFront,
Route 53) and resources returned identically by every region (S3 buckets, which
`ListBuckets` returns everywhere) are kept once and get no region from the
directory. The resource subject includes the
resource identifier as a link and a `resource_id` property. When the AWS
resource identifier is an ARN, generated evidence includes an AWS Resource
Explorer link using an exact `id:<arn>` search. AWS S3 bucket names are parsed
as `arn:aws:s3:::<bucket-name>` for Resource Explorer links. AWS Route53 hosted
zone identifiers such as `/hostedzone/Z123` are normalized to full ARNs such as
`arn:aws:route53:::hostedzone/Z123`.

`assessment.inventory_status` is `baseline` for resources found in the unfiltered
inventory run. If a policy returns a resource that is not present in the baseline,
the plugin still evaluates it as `non_compliant` and sets
`inventory_status` to `missing_from_baseline`.

#### Resource Identity

`resource.id` (and the `resource_id` label) is the first non-empty field from, in order:

1. the type's `resource_identity_fields`, when configured;
2. the built-in field list for the AWS type below: the ARN first, then the natural id, following
   the resource metadata of Cloud Custodian 0.9.49;
3. the generic fields `Arn`, `ARN`, `arn`, `Id`, `ID`, `id`, `InstanceId`, `instance_id`, `InstanceID`,
   `ResourceId`, `resource_id`, `Name`, `name`;
4. a SHA-256 of the whole resource, as a last resort.

| Type | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `aws.app-elb` | `LoadBalancerArn` |
| `aws.backup-plan` | `BackupPlanArn`, `BackupPlanName` |
| `aws.backup-vault` | `BackupVaultArn`, `BackupVaultName` |
| `aws.cache-cluster` | `ARN`, `CacheClusterId` |
| `aws.distribution` | `ARN`, `Id` |
| `aws.dynamodb-table` | `TableArn`, `TableName` |
| `aws.ebs` | `VolumeId` |
| `aws.ec2` | `InstanceId` |
| `aws.ecs-service` | `serviceArn` |
| `aws.efs` | `FileSystemArn`, `FileSystemId` |
| `aws.eks` | `arn`, `name` |
| `aws.firewall` | `FirewallArn`, `FirewallName` |
| `aws.hostedzone` | `Id` (normalized to an ARN) |
| `aws.iam-group` | `Arn`, `GroupName` |
| `aws.iam-policy` | `Arn`, `PolicyId` |
| `aws.iam-role` | `Arn`, `RoleName` |
| `aws.iam-user` | `Arn`, `UserName` |
| `aws.kms-key` | `Arn`, `KeyId` |
| `aws.lambda` | `FunctionArn`, `FunctionName` |
| `aws.log-group` | `arn`, `logGroupName` |
| `aws.rds` | `DBInstanceArn`, `DBInstanceIdentifier` |
| `aws.rds-cluster` | `DBClusterArn`, `DBClusterIdentifier` |
| `aws.s3` | `Name` |
| `aws.secrets-manager` | `ARN`, `Name` |
| `aws.sns` | `TopicArn` |
| `aws.sqs` | `QueueArn`, `QueueUrl` |
| `aws.transfer-server` | `Arn`, `ServerId` |
| `aws.wafv2` | `ARN`, `Id` |

The id never depends on the annotations Cloud Custodian adds to matched resources
(`c7n:MatchedFilters` and the like), so a check's matched resource is the same
resource as its inventory baseline record.

`provider` extraction rule:

- `aws.s3` -> `aws`
- non `<provider>.<resource>` formats -> `unknown`

### Policy Data

Any `policy_data` set on this plugin's block in the agent configuration is passed
to every policy evaluation and is available to Rego as `data.<key>`:

```yaml
plugins:
  cloud_custodian:
    # ...plugin settings as above...
    policy_data:
      allowed_regions:
        - eu-west-1
        - us-east-1
```
